stories.headline: Google's Gemini can now talk to you with a face that moves
stories.blurb: Gemini 3.8 Live now includes an animated avatar that lip-syncs and shows facial expressions while you talk to it. The feature is currently only available to Gemini Enterprise customers, but it marks Google's push to make AI conversations feel more like video calls than chat windows.
stories.why_it_matters: AI interfaces are shifting from text boxes to something closer to talking with a person on screen.
stories.original_headline: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar gives Google’s AI a face

stories.headline: Federal court upholds Pentagon ban on Anthropic's AI models
stories.blurb: A Washington appeals court ruled the Defense Department had sufficient evidence to justify blocking Anthropic's Claude models from military use over national security concerns. The company had challenged the blacklisting, arguing its AI safety practices made it suitable for government deployment.
stories.why_it_matters: First major legal precedent for how agencies can restrict commercial AI models from sensitive applications.
stories.original_headline: Anthropic’s Blacklisting by the Pentagon Was Legal, Federal Judges Rule

stories.headline: UK AI cloud startup Nscale raises $3.4B before US IPO
stories.blurb: Nscale, a British AI infrastructure company, secured $3.36 billion in convertible financing from investors including Third Point and Nvidia. The funding will finance a major expansion of AI data centers as the company prepares for a US public offering.
stories.why_it_matters: European AI infrastructure is scaling up to compete with hyperscalers for model training workloads.
stories.original_headline: Ahead of US IPO, British AI neocloud Nscale secures $3.36B in convertible financing

stories.headline: Sony and UMG sue Suno again, claiming its new model trained on pirated outputs
stories.blurb: Sony and Universal filed another lawsuit against AI music startup Suno, alleging its v6 model was trained on outputs from earlier models — which themselves learned from copyrighted songs ripped from YouTube. The labels argue this creates a 'laundering' chain that still violates their rights, even if no original tracks touched the latest training data.
stories.why_it_matters: Training new models on old model outputs might not dodge copyright claims.
stories.original_headline: Sony and UMG are suing Suno again

try_this_prompt.title: The strategy stress test
try_this_prompt.prompt: I'll describe our current strategy below. Now imagine three things happen simultaneously: our biggest competitor copies it tomorrow, our top performer quits, and our budget gets cut 30%. Tell me which part of the strategy survives intact and why that's the only part that actually mattered.
try_this_prompt.tool_hint: Separates real strategic bets from expensive wish lists.
